transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lisa Chen (Meridian - Head of AI), Mark Dobbs (Meridian - VP Eng), Ana Ruiz (Meridian - Cloud Architect)
Recording link: https://redwood.app/meetings/meridian-20270514 (note: placeholder)
Shared items: renewal deck (link), reserved-capacity-quote.xlsx (link), security-pack.zip (link)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Lisa: Lisa here.
[00:06] Mark: Mark, yep.
[00:08] Ana: Ana.
[00:10] Diego: Diego from Redwood.
[00:12] Samira: Great. We're here for the renewal + expansion check-in. We saw your note about needing more capacity for the fall peak and wanting an EU region. Wanted to walk through options and next steps.

[01:02] Lisa: Yup, quick context — our usage has been steady but Q4 marketing promos push up the batch jobs and chat throughput. We're forecasting a 40-50% peak increase and the current 4-GPU reserved pool is tight. Also legal wants eu-west-1 for some EU customer PII residency.

[01:45] Mark: Right, and performance stayed good in us-east but latency to EU is a concern for a subset of customers. We're evaluating dedicated nodes in eu-west vs routing to us-east with longer SLAs. Cost is a big factor.

[02:20] Diego: Okay — technical view: we can scale reserved pools in increments, and we also have burst options for short-term peaks. For eu-west-1 we can provision dedicated capacity, but there are two paths: 1) deploy a smaller dedicated pool in eu-west and keep main pool in us-east, or 2) add eu-west as a standby region with automatic routing and KV prefix caching across regions. Both have tradeoffs for cost and cold-start behaviors.

[03:02] Lisa: Can you clarify the cold-start?
[03:05] Diego: Sure. If you spin up new instances in eu-west, first requests may hit model load times unless you keep warmers or use pre-warmed burst capacity. There's also model variant pinning — if you're using quantized variants in eu-west, there's possible perf delta vs us-east.

[03:45] Samira: To map to your ask — sounds like you want a steady increase to 6 GPUs reserved plus eu-west capacity for residency. Does that sound right?

[03:58] Ana: Yes, 6 reserved is the baseline we think will cover steady-state; then a small eu-west pool (2 GPUs) to handle EU traffic and satisfy residency. We'd like the contract to extend to a 12-month renewal with price lock.

[04:20] Mark: Also want a clause for scaling to 8 GPUs if Q4 blows past projections — like a tiered price commitment for short notice scaling.

[04:35] Samira: Got it. On pricing we can do tiered reserved rates and burst pricing; I'll put together 12-month and 24-month options, with terms for in-term increases.

[05:10] Lisa: Security — we need SOC 2 Type II documentation, and clarity on KMS/HSM usage. Will data be encrypted at rest with a customer-managed key?

[05:30] Diego: Redwood supports customer KMS for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS — we have an option to bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for encryption at rest. For hosted we have managed keys, but we can discuss Private or VPC deployment if you require full BYOK/HSM. We'll share our security pack.

[06:05] Ana: We're leaning hosted+dedicated not Private due to ops overhead, but need proof points for encryption and audit logs. Also question about audit logs retention and access for compliance.

[06:40] Diego: Audit logs are configurable for dedicated; we can do longer retention as an add-on. We'll share the SOC2 report and a summary of audit log options.

[07:05] Mark: On performance: can you run a dedicated benchmark with our top-5 prompts? We want latency p95 under 220ms for chat completions and throughput to meet projected RPS.

[07:30] Diego: Yes. We'll need your prompt set and expected concurrency. We can run in us-east and eu-west to show differences. We'll include KV cache config and batching settings we recommend.

[08:10] Lisa: Good. Also curious about model fallbacks — if you don't have capacity in eu-west, can we automatically route to us-east? We can accept slightly higher latency but want failover.

[08:35] Diego: Absolutely. Smart routing + automatic fallback is standard. You can set latency vs cost policies; on fallback, we can also use a compatible model variant if exact model isn't available. We'll document the policy.

[09:00] Samira: Quick commercial note — renewal target is end of May; ideally get exec signoff week of May 24. If we can get the benchmark and updated quote before then, good chance to lock.

[09:22] Lisa: Yes that timeline works.

[10:00] [cross talk, background noise]
[10:30] Mark: A couple nitty gritty — SLA for dedicated: can we see the latency SLOs and penalty terms?

[10:45] Diego: We'll surface our SLA doc for Dedicated. Our SLOs vary by model profile and region; we'll attach model performance profiles with the quote. There's also an automatic failover guarantee for critical routes if you opt into multi-region.

[11:25] Ana: For eu data residency — does Redwood support tenancy separation? i.e., separate customer VPC in eu-west?

[11:40] Diego: For Dedicated we can do customer-isolated pools in a VPC. For hosted, it's multi-tenant but we have strict controls and SOC2 audited processes. If tenancy separation is required, dedicated VPC is the path.

[12:05] Samira: Sounds like actions: Diego will run perf tests; Samira will prepare pricing; Ana will send prompt set and Q4 RPS forecasts; Lisa will confirm exec sign-off timing. Anything else?

[12:25] Lisa: Can you include an option for a 24-month extension with deeper discounts? That's something the CFO will like.

[12:40] Samira: We'll include 12 and 24-month pricing. Tiered discounts for term and committed GPU counts.

[13:10] Mark: One more thing — how do upgrades work mid-term? If we want to move from 6->8 GPUs quickly, can you guarantee capacity?

[13:30] Diego: We have burst capacity and reserved capacity adjustments. For guaranteed immediate increase you can buy a short-term reserved burst or we can schedule a reserved increase; lead time depends on region capacity, but we can often do it within 48-72 hours in common regions. We'll note that in the quote.

[14:10] [few seconds of silence]
[14:25] Samira: Ok wrapping to recap — agreed: Redwood to produce updated quote (12 & 24 month), Redwood SE to run benchmarks in us-east + eu-west with your 5 prompts, share SOC2/KMS notes and audit log options, and Meridian to confirm exec sign-off timing.

[14:50] Lisa: Sounds good.

[15:00] Ana: I'll send the prompt set today.

[15:05] Diego: Great. I'll coordinate scheduling for the benchmark — likely later this week.

[15:20] Samira: Any competitor concerns we should address?

[15:25] Mark: CFO asked about Anthropic and OpenAI pricing comparisons — we'll send those benchmark prompts. Also saw a vendor called AcmeInference pitching dedicated on-prem as cheaper, but we want Redwood for the managed ops.

[16:00] Diego: We'll include a short comparison and show cost/e2e ops tradeoffs.

[16:25] [wrap up and pleasantries]
[16:40] Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the quote and docs. If anything comes up email or slack works.

[16:45] Lisa: Thanks.

[16:46] Mark: Thanks all.

[16:47] Ana: Bye.

End notes: transcript contains a few auto-transcription mishearings (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash' in other exports). Links shared above are placeholders.

Recap / Next steps (as discussed):
- Redwood (Samira): Send updated 12/24 month reserved capacity quote including 6 GPU baseline and 2 GPU eu-west pool; include tiered burst pricing and clause for quick scale to 8 GPUs; due 2027-05-18.
- Redwood (Diego): Run benchmarks in us-east + eu-west with Meridian-provided prompts; share perf traces, KV cache recommendations, and SOC2/KMS notes; due 2027-05-17 (bench scheduling) and results by 2027-05-21.
- Meridian (Ana): Provide top-5 prompts and Q4 RPS forecasts; due 2027-05-16.
- Meridian (Lisa): Confirm exec decision meeting window; due 2027-05-20.
